name: konvo
tagline: An iOS app that strips social down to direct messages, no feed, no posts.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A chat app is the easiest thing in the world to build and the hardest thing in the world to fill. The code is a websocket server, a message table, and a list of conversations: a competent agent does that before lunch. What you cannot generate is the other person sitting in the app waiting to reply, which is the entire product. Even for a two-person setup you inherit push notifications, background delivery, media handling, and an App Store review queue, none of which are one-session problems. Build a private group chat if you enjoy it, but understand you are building a room, not a party.
coreLoopDIY: Stands up a self-hosted realtime DM server with a web client where a small invite-only group can exchange text and images in one-to-one threads.
requirements: A small VPS or home server with a public hostname and TLS
Everyone you want to talk to willing to open a bookmarked web app instead of their existing messenger
Object storage or a local disk for image uploads
whatYouLose: The other people, which is the product
Mobile push notifications that actually arrive when the app is closed
A real iOS client, background sync, and share sheet integration
Read receipts, typing indicators, and delivery guarantees that hold up on flaky mobile networks
Whatever discovery or identity layer lets you message someone you do not already have a link for
moatNotes: Messaging is the textbook network-effects product: utility is strictly a function of who else installed it. A DMs-only positioning makes that dependence worse, not better, because there is no feed to browse while you wait for your friends to show up.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody pays for the message-passing. They pay, when they pay at all, for a place where the specific people they want to talk to already are, plus reliable mobile delivery that a self-hosted web app will never match. A private server you run is a chat app with a population of you and maybe three patient friends, and the first time a push notification silently fails to land, the experiment is over.
notes: The websocket server is an afternoon; the contact list is not. The moat is that a messenger is worth exactly as much as the number of people already inside it.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted, invite-only direct messaging app. Web only. No feed, no posts, no public profiles: one-to-one threads and nothing else.

Stack, no substitutions:
- TypeScript everywhere.
- Fastify HTTP server with the @fastify/websocket plugin.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/konvo.db, schema created on boot if missing.
- React + Vite + Tailwind for the client, served as static files by Fastify in production.
- Single repo, npm workspaces: packages/server and packages/web. One `npm run dev` starts both.

Data model:
- users: id, handle (unique, lowercase), display_name, password_hash (argon2), created_at.
- threads: id, user_a, user_b, unique on the sorted pair.
- messages: id, thread_id, sender_id, body (text), attachment_path (nullable), created_at, read_at (nullable).
- invites: token, created_by, used_by (nullable), expires_at.

Behaviour:
- No open signup. First boot reads ADMIN_HANDLE and ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env and creates one account. Any user can mint an invite link; registration requires a valid unused token.
- Session cookie, httpOnly, signed with COOKIE_SECRET from .env.
- Websocket per authenticated session. Server pushes new messages, typing indicators, and read receipts to connected peers. On reconnect the client pulls anything it missed by last-seen message id.
- Image uploads up to 10MB stored on local disk under ./data/uploads, served behind auth. Nothing else, no video, no voice notes.
- Thread list sorted by last message, unread count per thread, keyboard-first composer, Enter sends.

Explicitly out of scope: push notifications, native mobile apps, end-to-end encryption, group chats, search, reactions, telemetry, any third-party API.

Deliverables: working app, .env.example with every variable, a README covering `npm run dev`, production build, TLS via a reverse proxy, and how to back up the SQLite file. Seed script that creates two users and a short conversation so the UI is not empty on first run.
